# Lakebase Health checks

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_checks_doc.py from engine/src/lakebase_health/checks/**/*.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

64 checks: 31 telemetry, 29 Postgres and 4 API. The tested SQL and the reasoning behind each threshold are in [HEALTH_CHECKS.md](../HEALTH_CHECKS.md); this page is generated from the check files the engine runs.

## How to read this page

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Source | `telemetry`: SQL over the Delta copy of `system.lakebase` (all projects, no setup). `postgres`: SQL over the Postgres catalog on a running, enrolled read-write compute (never wakes a suspended compute). `api`: settings read from the Lakebase API. |
| Thresholds | Each check computes one number per object (the measure). The highest severity whose threshold the measure passes (strictly greater, or strictly less for checks where low is bad) is the finding's severity. No threshold passed means no finding. |
| Needs enrolment | Postgres checks run only on branches where the engine SP has a Postgres role (see the README, "Enroll a project for Postgres checks"). |
| Confidence | `low` when a guard fails, for example when the statistics window is shorter than 24 hours. |
| Superseded by | While a more specific finding is open for the same object, database or endpoint, this one is not reported (status `superseded`). It comes back if the other finding resolves. |
| Candidate fix | Placeholders in braces are filled from the finding's row; `{index_def_concurrently}` is the index definition (`pg_get_indexdef`) with `CONCURRENTLY` after `INDEX`. `ddl` and `setting` fixes become proposed actions when the fixer allowlist accepts the statement and its rollback; a fix with nothing to undo has a rollback note instead of a rollback. `manual` fixes are guidance only. |
| Fixer | Whether the fixer job can run the proposed action after approval. |

## Incidents

<a id="commit_quorum_wait"></a>

### commit_quorum_wait

**Commits wait for the WAL storage quorum**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.active_session_history`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 2; critical when measure > 5 |

**What it means.** Longest stretch (seconds) one statement spent in the SyncRep wait in the last 24 hours. The commit is written but the storage quorum (safekeepers) has not acknowledged it yet; normal is a few milliseconds (fleet p99 22 ms). While it waits the session keeps its row locks, so other writers queue behind it and can hit statement timeouts. This is a platform-side delay, not application contention: open a support case with the endpoint ID and the first_seen/last_seen window. hot_row_lock shows which waiters were blocked by these commits.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `safe`):

See the explanation above; there is no SQL for this one.

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="deadlocks"></a>

### deadlocks

**Deadlocks detected**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.database_counters`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 0; critical when measure > 2 |

**What it means.** Deadlocks in the last 2 hours per database. Lock rows in a consistent order, keep transactions short, retry on 40P01, and index foreign keys (missing_fk_index) to narrow lock scope. Details are in postgres_logs (40P01).

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.

<a id="gin_cleanup_lock_wait"></a>

### gin_cleanup_lock_wait

**Writes wait for a GIN pending-list cleanup**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.wait_event_counters`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 60; critical when measure > 600 |

**What it means.** Total seconds sessions waited on page locks in the last 24 hours (avg_wait_s per wait). On Lakebase this is the GIN pending-list cleanup lock: with fastupdate on, a write that finds the pending list over gin_pending_list_limit merges it into the index itself, and other writers queue behind it. See gin_pending_list for the index. Options, cheapest first: drop the index if it is unused on every compute; index only the text you search (and scope it, e.g. by tenant prefix with btree_gin); run gin_clean_pending_list on a schedule from one worker with a short lock_timeout; or set fastupdate = off so each write pays only for its own entries.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `safe`):

See the explanation above; there is no SQL for this one.

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="hot_row_lock"></a>

### hot_row_lock

**Writes wait on a row lock**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.active_session_history`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 3; critical when measure > 10 |
| Query scope | platform, engine and fixer roles are filtered out; one finding per query |

**What it means.** Longest time (seconds) a sampled statement waited for a row lock (tuple or transactionid) in the last 24 hours, per query. Each wait is joined to the blocking session's sample at the same instant to name the cause in likely_cause: commit_wait means the lock holder was itself waiting for the WAL storage quorum (platform side, see commit_quorum_wait); idle_in_transaction means the application holds a transaction open between statements (set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, commit sooner); active means real hot-key contention (shorten the transaction, avoid many writers updating the same row, batch per key, or use SKIP LOCKED for queues). not_sampled means the holder was not captured at that instant.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `safe`):

See the explanation above; there is no SQL for this one.

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="idle_in_tx_time"></a>

### idle_in_tx_time

**Sessions spend a lot of time idle in transaction**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.database_counters`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 5; critical when measure > 20 |

**What it means.** Share of session time spent idle inside an open transaction (24 h). Such sessions hold locks and block vacuum. Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (30-60 s) and fix application transaction scoping.

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.

<a id="statement_timeouts"></a>

### statement_timeouts

**Statements cancelled by statement_timeout**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.postgres_logs`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | info when measure > 1; warning when measure > 10; critical when measure > 100 |

**What it means.** Statements cancelled by statement_timeout (SQLSTATE 57014) in the last 24 hours. A cancelled write is lost unless the client retries. while_locking_row counts cancellations whose error context says the statement was waiting for a row lock; check hot_row_lock for who held it (application transaction vs. a commit stalled on the storage quorum). The rest timed out doing work: see top_db_time_query, storage_wait and gin_cleanup_lock_wait.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `safe`):

See the explanation above; there is no SQL for this one.

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="blocked_session"></a>

### blocked_session

**Session blocked by another session**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, once per endpoint (instance-wide catalogs) |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 60; critical when measure > 300 |

**What it means.** A session waiting on a lock held by another session (seconds blocked). Resolve the blocker first; durable fixes are idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, lock_timeout for DDL and short transactions.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `high`):

```text
Blocking pid {blocking_pid} ({blocking_state}); end it if safe: SELECT pg_terminate_backend({blocking_pid});
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="idle_in_transaction"></a>

### idle_in_transaction

**Session idle inside an open transaction**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, once per endpoint (instance-wide catalogs) |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 60; critical when measure > 300 |

**What it means.** A session that opened a transaction and went idle (seconds in that state). It holds its locks and snapshot, blocking writers and vacuum. Lower idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and fix the application.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `high`):

```text
After confirming with the session owner: SELECT pg_terminate_backend({pid});
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="long_transaction"></a>

### long_transaction

**Long-running transaction**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | incidents |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, once per endpoint (instance-wide catalogs) |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 300; critical when measure > 1,800 |

**What it means.** An active transaction open for more than 5 minutes (seconds). Long transactions hold locks and block vacuum. Set statement_timeout for application roles and split long batch jobs.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `high`):

```text
Investigate pid {pid}; cancel with SELECT pg_cancel_backend({pid}); if safe.
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

## Performance

<a id="disk_spill"></a>

### disk_spill

**Query spills sorts or hashes to disk**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.plan_history`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 0; critical when measure > 100 |
| Query scope | platform, engine and fixer roles are filtered out; one finding per query |

**What it means.** Executions in the last 24 h whose plan sorted on disk or used more than one hash batch, per query and role. Raise work_mem for that role (not globally), or add an index that delivers the sort order.

**Candidate fix** (kind `setting`, risk `moderate`, reversible, verified on a branch):

```sql
ALTER ROLE {role_ident} SET work_mem = '64MB';
```

Rollback:

```sql
ALTER ROLE {role_ident} RESET work_mem;
```

**Fixer.** No action is proposed: the statement is outside the fixer allowlist (only `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `ANALYZE` and `ALTER TABLE ... SET|RESET (autovacuum_*)` are accepted). The app shows the SQL marked "apply by hand".

<a id="plan_flip"></a>

### plan_flip

**Query switches between fast and slow plans**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.plan_history`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 2; critical when measure > 10 |
| Query scope | platform, engine and fixer roles are filtered out; one finding per query |

**What it means.** Ratio between the slowest and fastest median latency of a query's plan shapes on the same endpoint (7 days, >= 5 executions per shape). Fix statistics first; pin the good plan with pg_hint_plan only as a last resort.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `moderate`):

```text
ANALYZE the tables of query {object}; if the bad plan persists, pin the good one with a pg_hint_plan hint.
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

### query_regression

| | |
|---|---|

| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 1.5; critical when measure > 2 |

**What it means.** Mean latency in the last 24 h divided by the previous 6 days, per endpoint and query (>= 50 calls in each window). Correlate with recent DDL and statistics; fix with ANALYZE / CREATE STATISTICS before pinning plans.

<a id="row_misestimate"></a>

### row_misestimate

**Planner row estimates are far off**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.pg_stat_statements_counters`, `system.lakebase.plan_history`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | info when measure > 0; warning when measure > 10; critical when measure > 50 |
| Query scope | platform, engine and fixer roles are filtered out; one finding per query |

**What it means.** Share of the endpoint's database time (24 h) spent in read queries whose planner row estimate is off by 10x or more in the median execution (at least 50 calls, 1 s total and 3 sampled executions over 2 hours). The worst 10 by time are listed with estimated and actual rows. Run ANALYZE on the tables they read; add CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies, ndistinct) for correlated columns.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `safe`):

```text
ANALYZE the tables read by the queries in evidence.top_queries; consider CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies, ndistinct) on correlated columns.
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="sort_limit_waste"></a>

### sort_limit_waste

**Sort reads far more rows than the LIMIT returns**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.plan_history`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 10; critical when measure > 1,000 |
| Query scope | platform, engine and fixer roles are filtered out; one finding per query |

**What it means.** For plans topped by Limit with a Sort beneath, the largest row count read by a plan node divided by the rows the LIMIT returned (24 h). An index matching ORDER BY lets Postgres stop early instead of sorting everything.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `moderate`):

```text
Create an index matching the ORDER BY of query {object}, verified on a branch.
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

### storage_wait

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |

<a id="top_db_time_query"></a>

### top_db_time_query

**One query dominates database time**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.pg_stat_statements_counters`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 25; critical when measure > 50 |
| Query scope | platform, engine and fixer roles are filtered out; one finding per query |

**What it means.** Share of the endpoint's total execution time spent in one normalized query (24 h, at least 60 s total). Optimize it first: check its plan (disk_spill, row_misestimate) and indexes (seq_scan_heavy, missing_fk_index).

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.

<a id="stale_statistics"></a>

### stale_statistics

**Table statistics are missing or stale**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | performance |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, in every database |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 20; critical when measure > 100 |

**What it means.** Rows modified since the last ANALYZE as a share of live rows (100 when never analyzed). Stale statistics give the planner bad row estimates. Run ANALYZE; it is cheap and safe.

**Candidate fix** (kind `ddl`, risk `safe`, reversible, not verified on a branch):

```sql
ANALYZE {table_ident};
```

Rollback: not needed — ANALYZE only refreshes planner statistics.

**Fixer.** Yes: apply after approval. Not verifiable on a branch (no measurable query effect). Rollback: not needed (ANALYZE only refreshes planner statistics).

## Capacity

<a id="buffer_hit_rate"></a>

### buffer_hit_rate

**Postgres buffer cache hit rate low**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | capacity |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.database_counters`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | info when measure < 95; warning when measure < 90 |
| Superseded by | [`lfc_hit_rate`](#lfc_hit_rate) (same endpoint, while that finding is open and at least as severe) |

**What it means.** shared_buffers hit ratio per database (24 h). On Lakebase this is only the first cache tier in front of the local SSD cache, so judge lfc_hit_rate first; a low value here is informational unless the LFC rate is also low.

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.

<a id="connection_utilization"></a>

### connection_utilization

**Connections near the compute limit**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | capacity |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.compute_gauges`, `system.lakebase.database_gauges`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 70; critical when measure > 85 |

**What it means.** Peak open backends as a share of max_connections (24 h). Near the limit, new connections fail (53300). Use a client-side pool; with autoscaling the limit follows min(max CU, 8 x min CU), so raise min CU if needed.

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.

<a id="cpu_saturation"></a>

### cpu_saturation

**CPU saturated (p95 over 24 h)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | capacity |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.compute_counters`, `system.lakebase.compute_gauges`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 70; critical when measure > 85 |

**What it means.** p95 of CPU used versus the compute's logical CPUs over the last 24 hours. Sustained high CPU slows every query. Fix the top CPU queries first (see top_db_time_query); if CPU is pinned at the autoscaling maximum, raise max CU.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `moderate`):

```text
Optimize the top CPU queries, or raise autoscaling_limit_max_cu on {object}.
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="cu_sizing"></a>

### cu_sizing

**Compute size does not match the workload**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | capacity |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.compute_counters`, `system.lakebase.compute_gauges`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | info when measure > 0; warning when measure > 1 |
| Superseded by | [`cpu_saturation`](#cpu_saturation), [`lfc_hit_rate`](#lfc_hit_rate), [`working_set_vs_cache`](#working_set_vs_cache) (same endpoint, while that finding is open and at least as severe) |

**What it means.** Compute size against 7 days of telemetry. measure = 2 (undersized) when, for at least an hour at the largest size the compute reached, p95 CPU is above 85%, the working set exceeds the cache, or the cache hit rate is below 95% over at least 1M reads. measure = 1 (oversized) when an always-on compute of 2 CU or more sat at its minimum size with p95 CPU under 20%, a working set under 40% of the cache and a 99% hit rate. Short bursts, cold caches after scale-to-zero and pressure while still scaled down are ignored.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `moderate`):

```text
measure 2: raise max CU (min CU if cache-bound). measure 1: lower min CU or enable scale-to-zero on non-prod.
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="lfc_hit_rate"></a>

### lfc_hit_rate

**Local SSD cache hit rate below 99%**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | capacity |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.compute_counters`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure < 99; critical when measure < 95 |

**What it means.** Share of page reads served from the compute's local file cache instead of remote storage (24 h). OLTP needs 99%+. If the working set exceeds the cache, raise min CU (the cache follows the current size) or reduce pages read.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `moderate`):

```text
Raise min CU on {object} or index the queries reading the most pages.
```

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="storage_utilization"></a>

### storage_utilization

**Storage near its limit**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | capacity |
| Source | telemetry: `system.lakebase.compute_gauges`, read from the `raw_*` copy |
| Needs enrolment | No |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 70; critical when measure > 85 |

**What it means.** Used storage as a share of the limit (latest reading, 24 h). Write performance drops at the quota. Drop unused or duplicate indexes, reclaim bloat, archive cold data, or shorten the restore window.

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.

| | |

**What it means.** Peak 60-minute working set as a share of the local cache size (both in bytes, 24 h). Above 100% the data a workload touches no longer fits in cache. Raise min/max CU or shrink the working set (unused indexes, bloat).

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.

<a id="gin_pending_list"></a>

### gin_pending_list

**GIN index pending list near its limit**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | indexing |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, in every database |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | info when measure > 25; warning when measure > 50; critical when measure > 90 |
| Requires extension | `pgstattuple` (skipped as `extension_missing` without it) |

**What it means.** How full the GIN fast-update pending list is, as a percentage of gin_pending_list_limit, at the time of the check. When a write pushes the list past the limit, that write merges the whole list into the index itself, which can take seconds and blocks other writers (see gin_cleanup_lock_wait). Check idx_scan on every compute before keeping a large GIN index; then prefer a smaller index (only the searched text, scoped by tenant), a scheduled gin_clean_pending_list, or fastupdate = off if per-write cost is acceptable.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `safe`):

See the explanation above; there is no SQL for this one.

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="missing_fk_index"></a>

### missing_fk_index

**Foreign key without a supporting index**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | indexing |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, in every database |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 0; critical when measure > 1 GiB |

**What it means.** The referencing columns of a foreign key have no index (measure = child table size). Every DELETE or key UPDATE on the parent then scans the child while holding locks, a common cause of lock waits and deadlocks.

**Candidate fix** (kind `ddl`, risk `moderate`, reversible, verified on a branch):

```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY {index_name} ON {child_table} ({fk_columns});
```

Rollback:

```sql
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS {index_schema}.{index_name};
```

**Fixer.** Yes: verify on a branch, then apply after a second approval.

<a id="oversized_search_index"></a>

### oversized_search_index

**Large GIN/GiST search index**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | indexing |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, in every database |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 1 GiB; critical when measure > 10 GiB |

**What it means.** GIN or GiST index of 1 GB or more (measure = bytes). Every insert and update re-indexes the indexed text, so a search index over a whole document (for example a trigram index on value::text) costs write latency, storage, vacuum time and cache. If searches are always scoped (one user or tenant), a B-tree on the scope key plus filtering those rows is often enough: check idx_scan on every compute and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for the largest scopes on a branch. If a search index is needed, index only the searched text, put the scope key in it (btree_gin), and prefer full-text search (tsvector) over trigrams when word matching is enough.

**Candidate fix** (kind `manual`, risk `safe`):

See the explanation above; there is no SQL for this one.

**Fixer.** Guidance only (`manual`). The app shows it as text; nothing is proposed to the fixer.

<a id="privileged_roles"></a>

### privileged_roles

**Login role with powerful attributes**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | security |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, once per endpoint (instance-wide catalogs) |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | info when measure > 0; warning when measure > 1 |

**What it means.** A login role (not platform-managed) with BYPASSRLS, REPLICATION or CREATEROLE (measure = number of these). Keep such roles few and audited; use group roles for least privilege.

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.

<a id="public_schema_create"></a>

### public_schema_create

**Any role can create objects in a schema**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | security |
| Source | postgres: catalog query on the running read-write compute, in every database |
| Needs enrolment | Yes: a Postgres role for the engine SP with `pg_monitor` on the branch |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 0 |

**What it means.** PUBLIC holds CREATE on the schema, so every role can create objects there (an object-squatting and privilege-escalation risk). Revoke it and grant CREATE only to owning roles.

**Candidate fix** (kind `ddl`, risk `moderate`, reversible, not verified on a branch):

```sql
REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA {schema_ident} FROM PUBLIC;
```

Rollback:

```sql
GRANT CREATE ON SCHEMA {schema_ident} TO PUBLIC;
```

**Fixer.** No action is proposed: the statement is outside the fixer allowlist (only `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `ANALYZE` and `ALTER TABLE ... SET|RESET (autovacuum_*)` are accepted). The app shows the SQL marked "apply by hand".

<a id="password_roles"></a>

### password_roles

**Role uses a native Postgres password**

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | security |
| Source | api: Lakebase API inventory (`password_roles`) |
| Needs enrolment | No (the engine SP needs `CAN_USE` on the project) |
| Thresholds | warning when measure > 0 |

**What it means.** The role authenticates with a Postgres password instead of Databricks OAuth. Prefer OAuth roles, which leave no password to leak or rotate.

**Fixer.** No candidate fix; the finding is information only.
